faqs.a: The inverse rule of three solves inverse proportions: when one quantity grows, the other shrinks. If 4 workers need 6 hours, 3 workers need more time — 8 hours.
faqs.q: What is the inverse rule of three?

faqs.a: Direct: both rise or fall together — more apples cost more money. Inverse: one rises as the other falls — more workers finish faster.
faqs.q: What is the difference between direct and inverse proportion?

faqs.a: Multiply the two knowns and divide by the third: x = (A × B) / C. If A workers take B hours, C workers take (A × B) / C hours.
faqs.q: How do I solve an inverse proportion by hand?

faqs.a: It assumes every worker (or tap, or machine) contributes equally. In reality, coordination overhead can change the result — see the limitations.
faqs.q: Does doubling the workers really halve the time?

faqs.a: Not for inverse problems. The rule of three calculator for direct proportion covers those — here everything works in reverse.

inverse-rule-of-three-calculator.workedExample:
4 workers finish a job in 6 hours. How long do 3 workers take?

This is inverse: fewer workers means more time.
x = (A × B) / C = (4 × 6) / 3 = 24 / 3 = 8.

Answer: 8 hours.

The product 24 is the total work (worker-hours) and stays constant: 4 × 6 = 3 × 8.
